subject: Console: per-route economics alignment & exception handling
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: ACME Platform Team <platform@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 27 May 2028 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Console: per-route economics alignment & exception handling

Folks —

We need to align on a concise deliverable for the console workstream: a per-route economics view that shows tokenized cost, average latency, and tail latency (p95/p99) broken down by model_variant and tenant. This was flagged by ACME last week during the renewal call — they want better visibility into where cost is coming from and when the system is falling back to cheaper model variants.

High-level asks:
- A dashboard tile for product that surfaces: route_id, model_variant, tenant_id, token_count (by direction), cost_usd, avg_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, p99_latency_ms, fallback_count.
- An exception policy that generates a ticket when cost drift > 30% month-over-month for a tenant or when p99 latency increases > 200ms above baseline AND fallback_count > 0.
- Wire the tile to allow drilling into raw traces and the billing stream.

Open questions for this thread: who owns the telemetry mapping (events vs billing), can we backfill 30 days, and what is a safe canary window for infra changes that add route-level tags?

Attached a quick mock (mock-console-screenshot.png) to make the ask concrete.

Proposed owners: Marissa (data mapping / dashboard), Marcus (infra canary / SLOs), Irene (product validation & acceptance). If anyone needs a different assignment, reply with alternatives.

Thanks —
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Director, Observability & Console
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 27 May 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Console: per-route economics alignment & exception handling

Thanks Soojin — this looks good and useful for product calls. Quick notes on data:

- Telemetry sources: route events are in pathway-events (high-cardinality), billing is in billing-stream (aggregates per-minute). We'll need a nightly normalization join to align token_count and cost_usd by route_id + model_variant.
- Backfill: we can backfill 30 days but only at 1% sample rate for pathway-events due to volume; full fidelity is available in billing-stream. That means the initial dashboard needs a caveat about sampling for historical p95/p99.
- Schema: required fields from our side are route_id, model_variant, tenant_id, request_tokens, response_tokens, latency_ms, timestamp. I'll attach a small mapping CSV with column names and suggested joins (data-mapping.csv).

Action items I can take by EOD Tuesday:
1) Deliver mapping CSV and example SQL for the nightly join.
2) Create a lightweight Looker tile prototype (no drilldowns yet) for product to poke.

Question for Marcus: when you say "add route-level tags" — do you mean a runtime kernel change that will annotate requests, or an API-layer tag enrichment? The rollout and rollback plan depends on that.

—Marissa

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 29 May 2028 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Console: per-route economics alignment & exception handling

+1 on Marissa's mapping. A couple of infra notes:

- The most robust approach is to emit route tags at the API-layer (gateway) and carry them through the request path into our tracer and billing pipeline. Kernel-level instrumentation is heavier and would require maintenance across dedicated pools; avoid if possible.
- Canary plan: 2-week canary on a small percent of production traffic (start 1%, move to 10% after 48h if no regressions). We'll need a runbook for quick rollback; attaching a draft (canary-runbook.md).
- SLOs: define a per-route SLO (p99 < baseline + 200ms) and a cost SLO (monthly cost delta < 30% for a tenant without explicit config). Observability will need trace links and a sample of payloads for QA.

I'm happy to own the infra side and open the infra tickets — will do so after Marissa confirms the join keys. I also want to flag capacity implications if we decide to increase sampling to backfill more than 1%. That needs a billing estimate.

—Marcus

Thanks team — appreciate the quick turnaround. A couple of asks from ACME:

1) Can the canary be scheduled to start the week of June 12th? That gives our infra team time to coordinate network ACL adjustments.
2) For the drilldown experience, ACME would like direct access (read-only) to a tenant-scoped view in the console so our SREs can triage without a support ticket. Is that doable under the current RBAC plan?

If you can confirm the June 12th window and whether a read-only tenant view is possible, we'll sign off on the engagement timeline.

Best,
Joe Donner
Head of Platform, ACME Corp
